∡ denotes directed angles modulo 180°. Write A, B, C for the angles of triangle ABC and R = OA = OB = OC for its circumradius. Write D, E, F for the angles of triangle DEF. Let Ω be the circumcircle of triangle ABC, with center O; S lies on Ω. Let ω₁ be the circle (DEF); G lies on ω₁. Let U be a point other than A on the perpendicular from A to BC. Let V be a point other than D on the parallel to EF through D. Let X be the midpoint of BC. Let Y be the foot of the perpendicular from A to BC. Let Z be the reflection of H in BC. Let W be the reflection of A in O. Let L be the circumcenter of △ABH. Let M be the orthocenter of △ABC. Let N be the incenter of △ABC. Let T be the excenter of △ABC opposite A. Let X be an excenter of △ABC. Let Y be the centroid of △ABC. Let Z be the foot of the bisector from A in △ABC. Let W be the antipode of A on Ω. Let L be the antipode of D on ω₁. Let M be the point such that ABCM is a parallelogram. Let N be the point where the incircle of △ABC touches the side opposite A. Let T be the point where the excircle of △ABC opposite A touches the side opposite A. Let X be the center of the spiral similarity taking AB to CD. Let Y be the isogonal conjugate of P in △ABC. Let Z be the inverse of P in Ω. Let W be the pole of line BC with respect to Ω. Let L be the point of contact of a tangent from P to the circle (Q, QD). Let M be the midpoint of arc BC of Ω. Let N be the harmonic conjugate of D with respect to B and C. Let T be the intersection of the parallel to BC through D and AB. Let X be the intersection of the perpendicular to AC through H and the tangent at A to the circle centered at O. Let Y be the intersection of the isogonal of AP in ∠BAC and BC. Let Z be the second intersection of line AD with Ω. Let W be the second intersection of Ω with the circle (Q, QD).

Claim 1. ∡ABX = ∡XCA.

Proof. ∡ABX = ∡ACX = ∡XCA (inscribed angles in Ω; A, B, C, X concyclic).

∡DEG = ∡DFG = ∡QDE + 90° (∡DEG = ∡DFG, shown above; QD = QE = QF = QG, radii of Ω, HA = HB = HC, KA = KB = KC, AY tangent to Ω). ∡DEG = ∡DFG (D, E, F, G on ω₁). AB ⟂ CX (∡ABX = ∡XCA, shown in the proof of Claim 1; Claim 1). Apply the law of sines in △ABC. Apply the law of sines in △DEF (DE ⟂ EF).

AB = 2R·sin C    [law of sines in △ABC, sin∠AXB = sin C]

∡EDF = ∡EGF (D, E, F, G on ω₁). ∎
